headline: JPMorgan won't let outside AI agents access customer accounts or operate on their behalf
body: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon said the bank won't allow outside AI agents to access customer accounts and operate on their behalf, citing risks to the company and its customers. A spokeswoman told CNBC the bank currently blocks external agents from operating on behalf of retail customers, with no timeline for safeguards that would let agents interact directly with accounts. Agents can still access some customer data in a read-only fashion, such as balances, if Plaid or another connector has the user's credentials.
note: For finance teams, the distinction that matters is between reading account data and acting on it, and CNBC reports that agents can do the first but can't send money or pay a bill. Dimon said customers who use outside agents should understand there's a liability transfer.
correction: Headline dropped 'operate on their behalf', so it said less than the source. Body said 'citing risk to clients' and 'read some data through connectors like Plaid' with no condition. Note said the bank 'draws' a line the source does not attribute to it. Site Watch request, checked on the CNBC page: JPMorgan won't allow outside agents to access customer accounts and operate on their behalf, citing risks to the company and its customers; read-only access to balances applies only if Plaid or another connector has the user's credentials. Headline, body and note changed to match.

evidence.text: JPMorgan Chase won't allow outside artificial intelligence agents to access customer accounts and operate on their behalf, CEO Jamie Dimon said Tuesday, citing risks to the company and its customers as tech firms including Meta release autonomous assistants.

We're not going to allow just any … outside agent to come in inside the company, because it's just too risky for clients and for JPMorgan," Dimon told analysts on the bank's third-quarter earnings call.
A JPMorgan spokeswoman confirmed to CNBC that the bank currently blocks external AI agents from operating on behalf of retail customers.
There's no timeline for when the bank would have safeguards in place to allow agents to directly interact with customer accounts, the spokeswoman added.
That means that AI agents can access some customer data from Chase accounts in a read-only fashion, such as customer balances, if Plaid or another connector has the user's credentials.
But they can't send money or pay a bill — actions that make an agent useful.
If people are using them, they should understand the risk," Dimon said. "They should understand there's a liability transfer.
